title: The Cascade Cougar: A Black Cat Bicycles Fundraiser for Oakridge Trails Alliance – John Watson
content:
It’s been a whole year since the team at Paul Component Engineering in Chico built up a fundraiser bike! While John was in Chico on the long, slow road to the 2026 Made Bike Show, he hung out with the Paul crew and documented The Cascade Cougar. This Black Cat Bicycles drop-bar 29er is being raffled off as a fundraiser for Oakridge Trails Alliance. Read on for a project introduction by California Travis and a dusty gallery jam-packed with Chico magic from the team at Paul and John…

The Cascade Cougar is a hand-built drop bar 29er made by Black Cat Bicycles in California. It’s laced with a balleur build kit from various US manufacturers, and all proceeds go to the Oakridge Trails Alliance. It’s inspired by a 1992 dirt drop Salsa mountain bike. Let’s let California Travis take the mic…

Paul Hearts Builders

Hi, it’s your buddy Travis from Paul Component Engineering! We’re a machine shop full of bike nerds here in Chico, California, where we make things the hard way because we love high-quality American-made components. For the last 8 years, we’ve brought a super custom one-off bike to the Sea Otter Classic to highlight US manufacturing and raise money for various Bike/Trail/Public Land non-profits.

Paul Component Engineering founder Paul Price with his Dune Buggy…

This year we decided to skip Sea Otter and build a custom bike to show off at the Made Handmade Bike Show in Portland, Oregon. It just feels like Made is a bit more… our people. Custom framebuilders, smaller manufacturers, wild paint jobs… you know, obsessive bike-nerd creativity and eye-candy.

This year we were moving some bikes around the shop, and while moving Mr Paul’s 1992 Salsa drop-bar mountain bike to a different hanging hook, we were struck by how it’s simultaneously a snapshot of high-end custom bike parts circa 1992, but also, how ahead of its time this bike actually was.

We saw quite a few fat-tire drop-bar bikes on last weekend’s bike-camping trip that aren’t that far off in concept from Paul’s weird old Salsa. What if we built up a modern take on this bike? Not a replica, but a bike inspired by the versatility and spirit of this old Salsa.

Todd Ingermanson photos by Josh Becker

Black Cat Bicycles

It didn’t take long to think of which framebuilder we should approach for this project. Todd over at Black Cat Bicycles is known around California as “The Framebuilder’s Framebuilder”, because his bikes are such beautifully executed ridable artwork. He was making his own rocker-dropouts looong before the industry figured out why, and his sleeved lug-inspired fillet-brazing is almost hard to wrap your brain around. These frames aren’t cheap, but there are few builders that approach his obsessive attention to detail, experience, and unique creative approach.

The Build

After we sent Todd a video walkaround of ye olde Salsa to work off of, we started calling up our friends in the bike “Industry” for the best parts we could scare up. First, we called ourselves for as many polished PAUL parts as we could squeeze onto this bike (seatpost, seat collar, cranks, stem, disk brakes, and bar-ends).

Then we dialed up Astral Cycling in Eugene to lace up some shiny Serpentine rims to some White Industries hubs for us. Then we called White Industries directly for a headset, BTCHN’ Bikes for some HOT titanium drop-bars anodized to match, Brooks England for a cozy C17 saddle, Wolf Tooth for some nice American-machined pedals, Mad Monkey for a seat-bag, Madrone for a very specific derailleur (more on that in a bit), Teravail for some supple tan-wall tires, and Ron over at King Cage for some elegant hand-made H2O cages (he’ll be throwing those on the bike during the show).

Todd Ingermanson photos by Josh Becker

The Cascade Cougar

Todd understood the assignment. The frame showed up two weeks before the show, and is absolutely BEAUTIFUL, with a meticulous and time-consuming geometrically masked rainbow fade paint job, and chrome Black Cat logos. We were a bit nervous we wouldn’t have all the necessary components, but everything showed up at the last moment as promised, and with high-quality parts like this, the assembly was as easy as putting Legos together.

Using drop-bars with wide-range 1X mountain-bike gearing and cable-actuated brakes can be tricky, but we threw a Ratio Technology 12-speed adapter kit into an 11-speed SRAM “brifter”, and paired with a Madrone Jab rear derailleur they configured with a MTB clutch, a barrel adjuster, and Ratio specific pull, this bike shifts perfectly.

What’s Old is New

Yep, we build sweet bikes like this because it’s fun, and we are die-hard NERDS who just love the process of a custom build, but the main reason to build a wild bike like this is to raise money for somebody who deserves it, and since the MADE show is in Oregon, we decided to choose Oakridge Trails Alliance as the beneficiary.

Head on over to their GiveButter to donate for a chance to put this bike in your personal quiver. If you’ve ever mountain-biked in Oakridge, you know they’re doing the lord’s work. Thanks for attending my TED Talk. I hope you win this bike. Hugs, -Travis
